2	title: random functions
3	menu:
4	  main:
5	    parent: functions
6	---
7	
8	Functions for generating random values.
9	
10	### About randomness
11	
12	`gomplate` uses Go's [`math/rand`](https://pkg.go.dev/math/rand/) package
13	to generate pseudo-random numbers. Note that these functions are not suitable
14	for use in security-sensitive applications, such as cryptography. However,
15	these functions will not deplete system entropy.
16	
17	## `random.ASCII`
18	
19	Generates a random string of a desired length, containing the set of
20	printable characters from the 7-bit [ASCII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCII)
21	set. This includes _space_ (' '), but no other whitespace characters.
22	
23	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
24	### Usage
25	
26	```
27	random.ASCII count
28	```
29	
30	### Arguments
31	
32	| name | description |
33	|------|-------------|
34	| `count` | _(required)_ the length of the string to produce (number of characters) |
35	
36	### Examples
37	
38	```console
39	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.ASCII 8 }}'
40	_woJ%D&K
41	```
42	
43	## `random.Alpha`
44	
45	Generates a random alphabetical (`A-Z`, `a-z`) string of a desired length.
46	
47	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
48	### Usage
49	
50	```
51	random.Alpha count
52	```
53	
54	### Arguments
55	
56	| name | description |
57	|------|-------------|
58	| `count` | _(required)_ the length of the string to produce (number of characters) |
59	
60	### Examples
61	
62	```console
63	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.Alpha 42 }}'
64	oAqHKxHiytYicMxTMGHnUnAfltPVZDhFkVkgDvatJK
65	```
66	
67	## `random.AlphaNum`
68	
69	Generates a random alphanumeric (`0-9`, `A-Z`, `a-z`) string of a desired length.
70	
71	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
72	### Usage
73	
74	```
75	random.AlphaNum count
76	```
77	
78	### Arguments
79	
80	| name | description |
81	|------|-------------|
82	| `count` | _(required)_ the length of the string to produce (number of characters) |
83	
84	### Examples
85	
86	```console
87	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.AlphaNum 16 }}'
88	4olRl9mRmVp1nqSm
89	```
90	
91	## `random.String`
92	
93	Generates a random string of a desired length.
94	
95	By default, the possible characters are those represented by the
96	regular expression `[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]` (alphanumeric, plus `_`, `.`, and `-`).
97	
98	A different set of characters can be specified with a regular expression,
99	or by giving a range of possible characters by specifying the lower and
100	upper bounds. Lower/upper bounds can be specified as characters (e.g.
101	`"q"`, or escape sequences such as `"\U0001f0AF"`), or numeric Unicode
102	code-points (e.g. `48` or `0x30` for the character `0`).
103	
104	When given a range of Unicode code-points, `random.String` will discard
105	non-printable characters from the selection. This may result in a much
106	smaller set of possible characters than intended, so check
107	the [Unicode character code charts](http://www.unicode.org/charts/) to
108	verify the correct code-points.
109	
110	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
111	### Usage
112	
113	```
114	random.String count [regex] [lower] [upper]
115	```
116	
117	### Arguments
118	
119	| name | description |
120	|------|-------------|
121	| `count` | _(required)_ the length of the string to produce (number of characters) |
122	| `regex` | _(optional)_ the regular expression that each character must match (defaults to `[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]`) |
123	| `lower` | _(optional)_ lower bound for a range of characters (number or single character) |
124	| `upper` | _(optional)_ upper bound for a range of characters (number or single character) |
125	
126	### Examples
127	
128	```console
129	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.String 8 }}'
130	FODZ01u_
131	```
132	```console
133	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.String 16 `[[:xdigit:]]` }}'
134	B9e0527C3e45E1f3
135	```
136	```console
137	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.String 20 `[\p{Canadian_Aboriginal}]` }}'
138	ᗄᖖᣡᕔᕫᗝᖴᒙᗌᘔᓰᖫᗵᐕᗵᙔᗠᓅᕎᔹ
139	```
140	```console
141	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.String 8 "c" "m" }}'
142	ffmidgjc
143	```
144	```console
145	$ gomplate -i 'You rolled... {{ random.String 3 "⚀" "⚅" }}'
146	You rolled... ⚅⚂⚁
147	```
148	```console
149	$ gomplate -i 'Poker time! {{ random.String 5 "\U0001f0a1" "\U0001f0de" }}'
150	Poker time! 🂼🂺🂳🃅🂪
151	```
152	
153	## `random.Item`
154	
155	Pick an element at a random from a given slice or array.
156	
157	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
158	### Usage
159	
160	```
161	random.Item items
162	```
163	```
164	items | random.Item
165	```
166	
167	### Arguments
168	
169	| name | description |
170	|------|-------------|
171	| `items` | _(required)_ the input array |
172	
173	### Examples
174	
175	```console
176	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.Item (seq 0 5) }}'
177	4
178	```
179	```console
180	$ export SLICE='["red", "green", "blue"]'
181	$ gomplate -i '{{ getenv "SLICE" | jsonArray | random.Item }}'
182	blue
183	```
184	
185	## `random.Number`
186	
187	Pick a random integer. By default, a number between `0` and `100`
188	(inclusive) is chosen, but this range can be overridden.
189	
190	Note that the difference between `min` and `max` can not be larger than a
191	63-bit integer (i.e. the unsigned portion of a 64-bit signed integer).
192	The result is given as an `int64`.
193	
194	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
195	### Usage
196	
197	```
198	random.Number [min] [max]
199	```
200	
201	### Arguments
202	
203	| name | description |
204	|------|-------------|
205	| `min` | _(optional)_ The minimum value, defaults to `0`. Must be less than `max`. |
206	| `max` | _(optional)_ The maximum value, defaults to `100` (if no args provided) |
207	
208	### Examples
209	
210	```console
211	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.Number }}'
212	55
213	```
214	```console
215	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.Number -10 10 }}'
216	-3
217	```
218	```console
219	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.Number 5 }}'
220	2
221	```
222	
223	## `random.Float`
224	
225	Pick a random decimal floating-point number. By default, a number between
226	`0.0` and `1.0` (_exclusive_, i.e. `[0.0,1.0)`) is chosen, but this range
227	can be overridden.
228	
229	The result is given as a `float64`.
230	
231	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
232	### Usage
233	
234	```
235	random.Float [min] [max]
236	```
237	
238	### Arguments
239	
240	| name | description |
241	|------|-------------|
242	| `min` | _(optional)_ The minimum value, defaults to `0.0`. Must be less than `max`. |
243	| `max` | _(optional)_ The maximum value, defaults to `1.0` (if no args provided). |
244	
245	### Examples
246	
247	```console
248	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.Float }}'
249	0.2029946480303966
250	```
251	```console
252	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.Float 100 }}'  
253	71.28595374161743
254	```
255	```console
256	$ gomplate -i '{{ random.Float -100 200 }}'
257	105.59119437834909
258	```

7	
8	The `net` namespace contains functions that can help deal with network-related
9	lookups and calculations. Some of these functions return specifically-typed
10	values that contain additional methods useful for formatting or further
11	calculations.
12	
13	[RFC 4632]: http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4632
14	[RFC 4291]: http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4291
15	[`net`]: https://pkg.go.dev/net
16	
17	## `net.LookupIP`
18	
19	Resolve an IPv4 address for a given host name. When multiple IP addresses
20	are resolved, the first one is returned.
21	
22	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
23	### Usage
24	
25	```
26	net.LookupIP name
27	```
28	```
29	name | net.LookupIP
30	```
31	
32	### Arguments
33	
34	| name | description |
35	|------|-------------|
36	| `name` | _(required)_ The hostname to look up. This can be a simple hostname, or a fully-qualified domain name. |
37	
38	### Examples
39	
40	```console
41	$ gomplate -i '{{ net.LookupIP "example.com" }}'
42	93.184.216.34
43	```
44	
45	## `net.LookupIPs`
46	
47	Resolve all IPv4 addresses for a given host name. Returns an array of strings.
48	
49	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
50	### Usage
51	
52	```
53	net.LookupIPs name
54	```
55	```
56	name | net.LookupIPs
57	```
58	
59	### Arguments
60	
61	| name | description |
62	|------|-------------|
63	| `name` | _(required)_ The hostname to look up. This can be a simple hostname, or a fully-qualified domain name. |
64	
65	### Examples
66	
67	```console
68	$ gomplate -i '{{ join (net.LookupIPs "twitter.com") "," }}'
69	104.244.42.65,104.244.42.193
70	```
71	
72	## `net.LookupCNAME`
73	
74	Resolve the canonical name for a given host name. This does a DNS lookup for the
75	`CNAME` record type. If no `CNAME` is present, a canonical form of the given name
76	is returned -- e.g. `net.LookupCNAME "localhost"` will return `"localhost."`.
77	
78	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
79	### Usage
80	
81	```
82	net.LookupCNAME name
83	```
84	```
85	name | net.LookupCNAME
86	```
87	
88	### Arguments
89	
90	| name | description |
91	|------|-------------|
92	| `name` | _(required)_ The hostname to look up. This can be a simple hostname, or a fully-qualified domain name. |
93	
94	### Examples
95	
96	```console
97	$ gomplate -i '{{ net.LookupCNAME "www.amazon.com" }}'
98	d3ag4hukkh62yn.cloudfront.net.
99	```
100	
101	## `net.LookupSRV`
102	
103	Resolve a DNS [`SRV` service record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRV_record).
104	This implementation supports the canonical [RFC2782](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2782)
105	form (i.e. `_Service._Proto.Name`), but other forms are also supported, such as
106	those served by [Consul's DNS interface](https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/services/discovery/dns-dynamic-lookups#standard-lookup).
107	
108	When multiple records are returned, this function returns the first.
109	
110	A [`net.SRV`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/#SRV) data structure is returned. The
111	following properties are available:
112	- `Target` - _(string)_ the hostname where the service can be reached
113	- `Port` - _(uint16)_ the service's port
114	- `Priority`, `Weight` - see [RFC2782](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2782) for details
115	
116	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
117	### Usage
118	
119	```
120	net.LookupSRV name
121	```
122	```
123	name | net.LookupSRV
124	```
125	
126	### Arguments
127	
128	| name | description |
129	|------|-------------|
130	| `name` | _(required)_ The service name to look up |
131	
132	### Examples
133	
134	```console
135	$ gomplate -i '{{ net.LookupSRV "_sip._udp.sip.voice.google.com" | toJSONPretty "  " }}'
136	{
137	  "Port": 5060,
138	  "Priority": 10,
139	  "Target": "sip-anycast-1.voice.google.com.",
140	  "Weight": 1
141	}
142	```
143	
144	## `net.LookupSRVs`
145	
146	Resolve a DNS [`SRV` service record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRV_record).
147	This implementation supports the canonical [RFC2782](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2782)
148	form (i.e. `_Service._Proto.Name`), but other forms are also supported, such as
149	those served by [Consul's DNS interface](https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/services/discovery/dns-dynamic-lookups#standard-lookup).
150	
151	This function returns all available SRV records.
152	
153	An array of [`net.SRV`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/#SRV) data structures is
154	returned. For each element, the following properties are available:
155	- `Target` - _(string)_ the hostname where the service can be reached
156	- `Port` - _(uint16)_ the service's port
157	- `Priority`, `Weight` - see [RFC2782](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2782) for details
158	
159	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
160	### Usage
161	
162	```
163	net.LookupSRVs name
164	```
165	```
166	name | net.LookupSRVs
167	```
168	
169	### Arguments
170	
171	| name | description |
172	|------|-------------|
173	| `name` | _(required)_ The hostname to look up. This can be a simple hostname, or a fully-qualified domain name. |
174	
175	### Examples
176	
177	_input.tmpl:_
178	```
179	{{ range (net.LookupSRVs "_sip._udp.sip.voice.google.com") -}}
180	priority={{.Priority}}/port={{.Port}}
181	{{- end }}
182	```
183	
184	```console
185	$ gomplate -f input.tmpl
186	priority=10/port=5060
187	priority=20/port=5060
188	```
189	
190	## `net.LookupTXT`
191	
192	Resolve a DNS [`TXT` record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRV_record).
193	
194	This function returns all available TXT records as an array of strings.
195	
196	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
197	### Usage
198	
199	```
200	net.LookupTXT name
201	```
202	```
203	name | net.LookupTXT
204	```
205	
206	### Arguments
207	
208	| name | description |
209	|------|-------------|
210	| `name` | _(required)_ The host name to look up |
211	
212	### Examples
213	
214	```console
215	$ gomplate -i '{{net.LookupTXT "example.com" | data.ToJSONPretty "  " }}'
216	[
217	  "v=spf1 -all"
218	]
219	```
220	
221	## `net.ParseAddr`
222	
223	Parse the given string as an IP address (a
224	[`netip.Addr`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Addr)).
225	
226	Any of `netip.Addr`'s methods may be called on the resulting value. See
227	[the docs](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Addr) for details.
228	
229	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
230	### Usage
231	
232	```
233	net.ParseAddr addr
234	```
235	```
236	addr | net.ParseAddr
237	```
238	
239	### Arguments
240	
241	| name | description |
242	|------|-------------|
243	| `addr` | _(required)_ The IP string to parse. It must be either an IPv4 or IPv6 address. |
244	
245	### Examples
246	
247	```console
248	$ gomplate -i '{{ (net.ParseAddr "192.168.0.1").IsPrivate }}'
249	true
250	$ gomplate -i '{{ $ip := net.ParseAddr (net.LookupIP "example.com") -}}
251	  {{ $ip.Prefix 12 }}'
252	93.176.0.0/12
253	```
254	
255	## `net.ParsePrefix`
256	
257	Parse the given string as an IP address prefix (CIDR) representing an IP
258	network (a [`netip.Prefix`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Prefix)).
259	
260	The string can be in the form `"192.168.1.0/24"` or `"2001::db8::/32"`,
261	the CIDR notations defined in [RFC 4632][] and [RFC 4291][].
262	
263	Any of `netip.Prefix`'s methods may be called on the resulting value. See
264	[the docs](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Prefix) for details.
265	
266	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
267	### Usage
268	
269	```
270	net.ParsePrefix prefix
271	```
272	```
273	prefix | net.ParsePrefix
274	```
275	
276	### Arguments
277	
278	| name | description |
279	|------|-------------|
280	| `prefix` | _(required)_ The IP address prefix to parse. It must represent either an IPv4 or IPv6 prefix, containing a `/`. |
281	
282	### Examples
283	
284	```console
285	$ gomplate -i '{{ (net.ParsePrefix "192.168.0.0/24").Range }}'
286	192.168.0.0-192.168.0.255
287	$ gomplate -i '{{ $ip := net.ParseAddr (net.LookupIP "example.com") -}}
288	  {{ $net := net.ParsePrefix "93.184.0.0/16" -}}
289	  {{ $net.Contains $ip }}'
290	true
291	```
292	
293	## `net.ParseRange`
294	
295	Parse the given string as an inclusive range of IP addresses from the same
296	address family (a [`netipx.IPRange`](https://pkg.go.dev/go4.org/netipx#IPRange)
297	from the [`go4.org/netipx`](https://pkg.go.dev/go4.org/netipx) module).
298	
299	The string must contain a hyphen (`-`).
300	
301	Any of `netipx.IPRange`'s methods may be called on the resulting value.
302	See [the docs](https://pkg.go.dev/go4.org/netipx#IPRange) for details.
303	
304	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
305	### Usage
306	
307	```
308	net.ParseRange iprange
309	```
310	```
311	iprange | net.ParseRange
312	```
313	
314	### Arguments
315	
316	| name | description |
317	|------|-------------|
318	| `iprange` | _(required)_ The IP address range to parse. It must represent either an IPv4 or IPv6 range, containing a `-`. |
319	
320	### Examples
321	
322	```console
323	$ gomplate -i '{{ (net.ParseRange "192.168.0.0-192.168.0.255").To }}'
324	192.168.0.255
325	$ gomplate -i '{{ $range := net.ParseRange "1.2.3.0-1.2.3.233" -}}
326	  {{ $range.Prefixes }}'
327	[1.2.3.0/25 1.2.3.128/26 1.2.3.192/27 1.2.3.224/29 1.2.3.232/31]
328	```
329	
330	## `net.CIDRHost` _(experimental)_
331	**Experimental:** This function is [_experimental_][experimental] and may be enabled with the [`--experimental`][experimental] flag.

336	
337	The IP network can be in the form `"192.168.1.0/24"` or `"2001::db8::/32"`,
338	the CIDR notations defined in [RFC 4632][] and [RFC 4291][].
339	
340	Any of `netip.Addr`'s methods may be called on the resulting value. See
341	[the docs](https://pkg.go.dev/net/netip#Addr) for details.
342	
343	_Added in gomplate [v3.11.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.11.0)_

346	```

348	```
349	```

351	```

355	| name | description |

1	// Package num provides shared number coercion helpers used by the template
2	// function namespaces. The semantics mirror the observed behaviour of the
3	// reference tool: strings are parsed leniently (base-prefix aware for ints),
4	// booleans coerce to 0/1, and floats truncate toward zero when converted to
5	// integers.
6	package num
7	
8	import (
9		"encoding/json"
10		"strconv"
11		"strings"
12	)
13	
14	// IsFloat reports whether v should be treated as a floating-point value:
15	// either it is a float type, or it is a string (or json.Number) that only
16	// parses as a float (e.g. contains '.', 'e' or a float suffix).
17	func IsFloat(v any) bool {
18		switch n := v.(type) {
19		case float32, float64:
20			return true
21		case int, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64:
22			return false
23		case bool:
24			return false
25		case string:
26			return stringIsFloat(n)
27		case json.Number:
28			return stringIsFloat(n.String())
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	func stringIsFloat(s string) bool {
34		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
35		if s == "" {
36			return false
37		}
38		if _, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 0, 64); err == nil {
39			return false
40		}
41		_, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64)
42		return err == nil
43	}
44	
45	// ToInt64 coerces v to an int64 using lenient parsing.
46	func ToInt64(v any) int64 {
47		switch n := v.(type) {
48		case int:
49			return int64(n)
50		case int8:
51			return int64(n)
52		case int16:
53			return int64(n)
54		case int32:
55			return int64(n)
56		case int64:
57			return n
58		case uint:
59			return int64(n)
60		case uint8:
61			return int64(n)
62		case uint16:
63			return int64(n)
64		case uint32:
65			return int64(n)
66		case uint64:
67			return int64(n)
68		case float32:
69			return int64(n)
70		case float64:
71			return int64(n)
72		case bool:
73			if n {
74				return 1
75			}
76			return 0
77		case string:
78			return stringToInt64(n)
79		case json.Number:
80			return stringToInt64(n.String())
81		}
82		return 0
83	}
84	
85	func stringToInt64(s string) int64 {
86		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
87		if i, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 0, 64); err == nil {
88			return i
89		}
90		if f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64); err == nil {
91			return int64(f)
92		}
93		return 0
94	}
95	
96	// ToUint64 coerces v to a uint64 using lenient parsing.
97	func ToUint64(v any) uint64 {
98		return uint64(ToInt64(v))
99	}
100	
101	// ToFloat64 coerces v to a float64 using lenient parsing.
102	func ToFloat64(v any) float64 {
103		switch n := v.(type) {
104		case int:
105			return float64(n)
106		case int8:
107			return float64(n)
108		case int16:
109			return float64(n)
110		case int32:
111			return float64(n)
112		case int64:
113			return float64(n)
114		case uint:
115			return float64(n)
116		case uint8:
117			return float64(n)
118		case uint16:
119			return float64(n)
120		case uint32:
121			return float64(n)
122		case uint64:
123			return float64(n)
124		case float32:
125			return float64(n)
126		case float64:
127			return n
128		case bool:
129			if n {
130				return 1
131			}
132			return 0
133		case string:
134			return stringToFloat64(n)
135		case json.Number:
136			return stringToFloat64(n.String())
137		}
138		return 0
139	}
140	
141	func stringToFloat64(s string) float64 {
142		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
143		if i, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 0, 64); err == nil {
144			return float64(i)
145		}
146		if f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64); err == nil {
147			return f
148		}
149		return 0
150	}

7	
8	This namespace wraps the [`github.com/hashicorp/go-sockaddr`](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-sockaddr)
9	package, which makes it easy to discover information about a system's network
10	interfaces.
11	
12	These functions are _partly_ documented here for convenience, but the canonical
13	documentation is at https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hashicorp/go-sockaddr.
14	
15	Aside from some convenience functions, the general method of working with these
16	functions is through a _pipeline_. There are _source_ functions, which select
17	interfaces ([`IfAddr`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hashicorp/go-sockaddr#IfAddr)),
18	and there are functions to further filter, refine, and finally to select
19	the specific attributes you're interested in.
20	
21	To demonstrate how this can be used, here's an example that lists all of the IPv4 addresses available on the system:
22	
23	_in.tmpl:_
24	```
25	{{ range (sockaddr.GetAllInterfaces | sockaddr.Include "type" "ipv4") -}}
26	{{ . | sockaddr.Attr "address" }}
27	{{end}}
28	```
29	
30	```console
31	$ gomplate -f in.tmpl
32	127.0.0.1
33	10.0.0.8
34	132.79.79.79
35	```
36	
37	[RFC 1918]: http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1918
38	[RFC 6890]: http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6890
39	
40	## `sockaddr.GetAllInterfaces`
41	
42	Iterates over all available network interfaces and finds all available IP
43	addresses on each interface and converts them to `sockaddr.IPAddrs`, and returning
44	the result as an array of `IfAddr`.
45	
46	Should be piped through a further function to refine and extract attributes.
47	
48	_Added in gomplate [v2.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.4.0)_
49	### Usage
50	
51	```
52	sockaddr.GetAllInterfaces
53	```
54	
55	
56	## `sockaddr.GetDefaultInterfaces`
57	
58	Returns `IfAddrs` of the addresses attached to the default route.
59	
60	Should be piped through a further function to refine and extract attributes.
61	
62	_Added in gomplate [v2.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.4.0)_
63	### Usage

66	sockaddr.GetDefaultInterfaces
67	```

70	## `sockaddr.GetPrivateInterfaces`
71	
72	Returns an array of `IfAddr`s containing every IP that matches
73	[RFC 6890][], is attached to the interface with
74	the default route, and is a forwardable IP address.
75	
76	**Note:** [RFC 6890][] is a more exhaustive version of [RFC 1918][]
77	because it spans IPv4 and IPv6, however it does permit the inclusion of likely
78	undesired addresses such as multicast, therefore our definition of a "private"
79	address also excludes non-forwardable IP addresses (as defined by the IETF).
80	
81	Should be piped through a further function to refine and extract attributes.
82	
83	_Added in gomplate [v2.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.4.0)_
84	### Usage
85	
86	```
87	sockaddr.GetPrivateInterfaces
88	```
89	
90	
91	## `sockaddr.GetPublicInterfaces`
92	
93	Returns an array of `IfAddr`s that do not match [RFC 6890][],
94	are attached to the default route, and are forwardable.
95	
96	Should be piped through a further function to refine and extract attributes.
97	
98	_Added in gomplate [v2.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.4.0)_
99	### Usage
100	
101	```
102	sockaddr.GetPublicInterfaces
103	```
104	
105	
106	## `sockaddr.Sort`
107	
108	Returns an array of `IfAddr`s sorted based on the given selector. Multiple sort
109	clauses can be passed in as a comma-delimited list without whitespace.
110	
111	### Selectors
112	
113	The valid selectors are:
114	
115	| selector | sorts by... |
116	|----------|-------------|
117	| `address` | the network address |
118	| `default` | whether or not the `IfAddr` has a default route |
119	| `name` | the interface name |
120	| `port` | the port, if included in the `IfAddr` |
121	| `size` | the size of the network mask, smaller mask (larger number of hosts per network) to largest (e.g. a /24 sorts before a /32) |
122	| `type` | the type of the `IfAddr`. Order is Unix, IPv4, then IPv6 |
123	
124	Each of these selectors sort _ascending_, but a _descending_ sort may be chosen
125	by prefixing the selector with a `-` (e.g. `-address`). You may prefix with a `+`
126	to make explicit that the sort is ascending.
127	
128	`IfAddr`s that are not comparable will be at the end of the list and in a
129	non-deterministic order.
130	
131	_Added in gomplate [v2.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.4.0)_
132	### Usage
133	
134	```
135	sockaddr.Sort selector <array-of-IfAddrs>
136	```
137	```
138	<array-of-IfAddrs> | sockaddr.Sort selector
139	```
140	
141	### Arguments
142	
143	| name | description |
144	|------|-------------|
145	| `selector` | _(required)_ which selector to use (see above for values) |
146	| `<array-of-IfAddrs>` | _(required)_ the array of `IfAddr`s to sort |
147	
148	### Examples
149	
150	To sort first by interface name, then by address (descending):
151	```console
152	$ gomplate -i '{{ sockaddr.GetAllInterfaces | sockaddr.Sort "name,-address" }}'
153	```
154	
155	## `sockaddr.Exclude`
156	
157	Returns an array of `IfAddr`s filtered by interfaces that do not match the given
158	selector's value.
159	
160	### Selectors
161	
162	The valid selectors are:
163	
164	| selector | excludes by... |
165	|----------|-------------|
166	| `address` | the network address |
167	| `flag` | the specified flags (see below) |
168	| `name` | the interface name |
169	| `network` | being part of the given IP network (in net/mask format) |
170	| `port` | the port, if included in the `IfAddr` |
171	| `rfc` | being included in networks defined by the given RFC. See [the source code](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-sockaddr/blob/master/rfc.go#L38) for a list of valid RFCs |
172	| `size` | the size of the network mask, as number of bits (e.g. `"24"` for a /24) |
173	| `type` | the type of the `IfAddr`. `unix`, `ipv4`, or `ipv6` |
174	
175	#### supported flags
176	
177	These flags are supported by the `flag` selector:
178	`broadcast`, `down`, `forwardable`, `global unicast`, `interface-local multicast`,
179	`link-local multicast`, `link-local unicast`, `loopback`, `multicast`, `point-to-point`,
180	`unspecified`, `up`
181	
182	_Added in gomplate [v2.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.4.0)_
183	### Usage
184	
185	```
186	sockaddr.Exclude selector value <array-of-IfAddrs>
187	```
188	```
189	<array-of-IfAddrs> | sockaddr.Exclude selector value
190	```
191	
192	### Arguments
193	
194	| name | description |
195	|------|-------------|
196	| `selector` | _(required)_ which selector to use (see above for values) |
197	| `value` | _(required)_ the selector value to exclude |
198	| `<array-of-IfAddrs>` | _(required)_ the array of `IfAddr`s to consider |
199	
200	### Examples
201	
202	To exclude all IPv6 interfaces:
203	```console
204	$ gomplate -i '{{ sockaddr.GetAllInterfaces | sockaddr.Exclude "type" "ipv6" }}'
205	```

1	// Package num provides shared number coercion helpers used by the template
2	// function namespaces. The semantics mirror the observed behaviour of the
3	// reference tool: strings are parsed leniently (base-prefix aware for ints),
4	// booleans coerce to 0/1, and floats truncate toward zero when converted to
5	// integers.
6	package num
7	
8	import (
9		"encoding/json"
10		"strconv"
11		"strings"
12	)
13	
14	// IsFloat reports whether v should be treated as a floating-point value:
15	// either it is a float type, or it is a string (or json.Number) that only
16	// parses as a float (e.g. contains '.', 'e' or a float suffix).
17	func IsFloat(v any) bool {
18		switch n := v.(type) {
19		case float32, float64:
20			return true
21		case int, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64:
22			return false
23		case bool:
24			return false
25		case string:
26			return stringIsFloat(n)
27		case json.Number:
28			return stringIsFloat(n.String())
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	func stringIsFloat(s string) bool {
34		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
35		if s == "" {
36			return false
37		}
38		if _, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 0, 64); err == nil {
39			return false
40		}
41		_, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64)
42		return err == nil
43	}
44	
45	// ToInt64 coerces v to an int64 using lenient parsing.
46	func ToInt64(v any) int64 {
47		switch n := v.(type) {
48		case int:
49			return int64(n)
50		case int8:
51			return int64(n)
52		case int16:
53			return int64(n)
54		case int32:
55			return int64(n)
56		case int64:
57			return n
58		case uint:
59			return int64(n)
60		case uint8:
61			return int64(n)
62		case uint16:
63			return int64(n)
64		case uint32:
65			return int64(n)
66		case uint64:
67			return int64(n)
68		case float32:
69			return int64(n)
70		case float64:
71			return int64(n)
72		case bool:
73			if n {
74				return 1
75			}
76			return 0
77		case string:
78			return stringToInt64(n)
79		case json.Number:
80			return stringToInt64(n.String())
81		}
82		return 0
83	}
84	
85	func stringToInt64(s string) int64 {
86		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
87		if i, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 0, 64); err == nil {
88			return i
89		}
90		if f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64); err == nil {
91			return int64(f)
92		}
93		return 0
94	}

122		case uint64:

124		case float32:
125			return float64(n)

133		case string:
134			return stringToFloat64(n)

137		}

7	
8	gomplate's path functions are split into 2 namespaces:
9	- `path`, which is useful for manipulating slash-based (`/`) paths, such as in URLs
10	- `filepath`, which should be used for local filesystem paths, especially when Windows paths may be involved.
11	
12	This page documents the `path` namespace - see also the [`filepath`](../filepath) documentation.
13	
14	These functions are wrappers for Go's [`path`](https://pkg.go.dev/path/) and [`path/filepath`](https://pkg.go.dev/path/filepath/) packages.
15	
16	## `path.Base`
17	
18	Returns the last element of path. Trailing slashes are removed before extracting the last element. If the path is empty, Base returns `.`. If the path consists entirely of slashes, Base returns `/`.
19	
20	A wrapper for Go's [`path.Base`](https://pkg.go.dev/path/#Base) function.
21	
22	_Added in gomplate [v2.7.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.7.0)_
23	### Usage
24	
25	```
26	path.Base path
27	```
28	```
29	path | path.Base
30	```
31	
32	### Arguments
33	
34	| name | description |
35	|------|-------------|
36	| `path` | _(required)_ The input path |
37	
38	### Examples
39	
40	```console
41	$ gomplate -i '{{ path.Base "/tmp/foo" }}'
42	foo
43	```

56	```

59	```

64	|------|-------------|
65	| `path` | _(required)_ The input path |

72	```

84	path.Dir path
85	```

87	path | path.Dir

113	path.Ext path

115	```

118	
119	### Arguments
120	
121	| name | description |
122	|------|-------------|
123	| `path` | _(required)_ The input path |

125	### Examples
126

10	## `file.Exists`

112	
113	Reads a directory and lists the files and directories contained within.

145	
146	Returns a [`os.FileInfo`](https://pkg.go.dev/os/#FileInfo) describing the named path.

174	## `file.Walk`
175	
176	Like a recursive [`file.ReadDir`](#filereaddir), recursively walks the file tree rooted at `path`, and returns an array of all files and directories contained within.
177	
178	The files are walked in lexical order, which makes the output deterministic but means that for very large directories can be inefficient.
179	
180	Walk does not follow symbolic links.
181	
182	Similar to Go's [`filepath.Walk`](https://pkg.go.dev/path/filepath/#Walk) function.
183	
184	_Added in gomplate [v2.6.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.6.0)_
185	### Usage
186	
187	```
188	file.Walk path
189	```
190	```
191	path | file.Walk
192	```
193	
194	### Arguments
195	
196	| name | description |
197	|------|-------------|
198	| `path` | _(required)_ The path |
199	
200	### Examples
201	
202	```console
203	$ tree /tmp/foo
204	/tmp/foo
205	├── one
206	├── sub
207	│   ├── one
208	│   └── two
209	├── three
210	└── two
211	
212	1 directory, 5 files
213	$ gomplate -i '{{ range file.Walk "/tmp/foo" }}{{ if not (file.IsDir .) }}{{.}} is a file{{"\n"}}{{end}}{{end}}'
214	/tmp/foo/one is a file
215	/tmp/foo/sub/one is a file
216	/tmp/foo/sub/two is a file
217	/tmp/foo/three is a file
218	/tmp/foo/two is a file
219	```

221	## `file.Write`
222	
223	Write the given data to the given file. If the file exists, it will be overwritten.
224	
225	For increased security, `file.Write` will only write to files which are contained within the current working directory. Attempts to write elsewhere will fail with an error.
226	
227	Non-existing directories in the output path will be created.
228	
229	If the data is a byte array (`[]byte`), it will be written as-is. Otherwise, it will be converted to a string before being written.
230	
231	_Added in gomplate [v2.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.4.0)_
232	### Usage
233	
234	```
235	file.Write filename data
236	```
237	```
238	data | file.Write filename
239	```
240	
241	### Arguments
242	
243	| name | description |
244	|------|-------------|
245	| `filename` | _(required)_ The name of the file to write to |
246	| `data` | _(required)_ The data to write |
247	
248	### Examples
249	
250	```console
251	$ gomplate -i '{{ file.Write "/tmp/foo" "hello world" }}'
252	$ cat /tmp/foo
253	hello world
254	```

9	## `base64.Encode`
10	
11	Encode data as a Base64 string. Specifically, this uses the standard Base64 encoding as defined in [RFC4648 §4](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4648#section-4) (and _not_ the URL-safe encoding).
12	
13	_Added in gomplate [v1.8.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.8.0)_

15	
16	```
17	base64.Encode input
18	```

20	input | base64.Encode
21	```

23	### Arguments
24	
25	| name | description |
26	|------|-------------|
27	| `input` | _(required)_ The data to encode. Can be a string, a byte array, or a buffer. Other types will be converted to strings first. |
28	
29	### Examples
30	
31	```console
32	$ gomplate -i '{{ base64.Encode "hello world" }}'
33	aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=
34	```

44	This function outputs the data as a string, so it may not be appropriate
45	for decoding binary data. Use [`base64.DecodeBytes`](#base64decodebytes)

61	|------|-------------|
62	| `input` | _(required)_ The base64 string to decode |
63	
64	### Examples
65	
66	```console
67	$ gomplate -i '{{ base64.Decode "aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=" }}'

69	```

73	```

75	## `base64.DecodeBytes`
76	
77	Decode a Base64 string. This supports both standard ([RFC4648 §4](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4648#section-4)) and URL-safe ([RFC4648 §5](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4648#section-5)) encodings.

79	This function outputs the data as a byte array, so it's most useful for
80	outputting binary data that will be processed further.
81	Use [`base64.Decode`](#base64decode) to output a plain string.

90	### Arguments

95	
96	### Examples

98	```console
99	$ gomplate -i '{{ base64.DecodeBytes "aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=" }}'

101	```

1	// Package num provides shared number coercion helpers used by the template
2	// function namespaces. The semantics mirror the observed behaviour of the
3	// reference tool: strings are parsed leniently (base-prefix aware for ints),
4	// booleans coerce to 0/1, and floats truncate toward zero when converted to
5	// integers.
6	package num
7	
8	import (
9		"encoding/json"
10		"strconv"
11		"strings"
12	)
13	
14	// IsFloat reports whether v should be treated as a floating-point value:
15	// either it is a float type, or it is a string (or json.Number) that only
16	// parses as a float (e.g. contains '.', 'e' or a float suffix).
17	func IsFloat(v any) bool {
18		switch n := v.(type) {
19		case float32, float64:
20			return true
21		case int, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64:
22			return false
23		case bool:
24			return false
25		case string:
26			return stringIsFloat(n)
27		case json.Number:
28			return stringIsFloat(n.String())
29		}
30		return false
31	}
32	
33	func stringIsFloat(s string) bool {
34		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
35		if s == "" {
36			return false
37		}
38		if _, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 0, 64); err == nil {
39			return false
40		}
41		_, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64)
42		return err == nil
43	}
44	
45	// ToInt64 coerces v to an int64 using lenient parsing.
46	func ToInt64(v any) int64 {
47		switch n := v.(type) {
48		case int:
49			return int64(n)
50		case int8:
51			return int64(n)
52		case int16:
53			return int64(n)
54		case int32:
55			return int64(n)
56		case int64:
57			return n
58		case uint:
59			return int64(n)
60		case uint8:
61			return int64(n)
62		case uint16:
63			return int64(n)
64		case uint32:
65			return int64(n)
66		case uint64:
67			return int64(n)
68		case float32:
69			return int64(n)
70		case float64:
71			return int64(n)
72		case bool:
73			if n {
74				return 1
75			}
76			return 0
77		case string:
78			return stringToInt64(n)
79		case json.Number:
80			return stringToInt64(n.String())
81		}
82		return 0
83	}
84	
85	func stringToInt64(s string) int64 {
86		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
87		if i, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 0, 64); err == nil {
88			return i
89		}
90		if f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64); err == nil {
91			return int64(f)
92		}
93		return 0
94	}
95	
96	// ToUint64 coerces v to a uint64 using lenient parsing.
97	func ToUint64(v any) uint64 {
98		return uint64(ToInt64(v))
99	}
100	
101	// ToFloat64 coerces v to a float64 using lenient parsing.
102	func ToFloat64(v any) float64 {
103		switch n := v.(type) {
104		case int:
105			return float64(n)
106		case int8:
107			return float64(n)
108		case int16:
109			return float64(n)
110		case int32:
111			return float64(n)
112		case int64:
113			return float64(n)
114		case uint:
115			return float64(n)
116		case uint8:
117			return float64(n)
118		case uint16:
119			return float64(n)
120		case uint32:
121			return float64(n)
122		case uint64:
123			return float64(n)
124		case float32:
125			return float64(n)
126		case float64:
127			return n
128		case bool:
129			if n {
130				return 1
131			}
132			return 0
133		case string:
134			return stringToFloat64(n)
135		case json.Number:
136			return stringToFloat64(n.String())
137		}
138		return 0
139	}
140	
141	func stringToFloat64(s string) float64 {
142		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
143		if i, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 0, 64); err == nil {

11	## `env.Getenv`
12	
13	**Alias:** `getenv`
14	
15	Exposes the [os.Getenv](https://pkg.go.dev/os/#Getenv) function.
16	
17	Retrieves the value of the environment variable named by the key. If the
18	variable is unset, but the same variable ending in `_FILE` is set, the contents
19	of the file will be returned. Otherwise the provided default (or an empty
20	string) is returned.
21	
22	This is a more forgiving alternative to using `.Env`, since missing keys will
23	return an empty string, instead of panicking.
24	
25	The `_FILE` fallback is especially useful for use with [12-factor][]-style
26	applications configurable only by environment variables, and especially in
27	conjunction with features like [Docker Secrets][].
28	
29	_Added in gomplate [v0.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v0.2.0)_
30	### Usage
31	
32	```
33	env.Getenv var [default]
34	```
35	
36	### Arguments
37	
38	| name | description |
39	|------|-------------|
40	| `var` | _(required)_ the environment variable name |
41	| `default` | _(optional)_ the default |
42	
43	### Examples
44	
45	```console
46	$ gomplate -i 'Hello, {{env.Getenv "USER"}}'
47	Hello, hairyhenderson
48	$ gomplate -i 'Hey, {{getenv "FIRSTNAME" "you"}}!'
49	Hey, you!
50	```
51	```console
52	$ echo "safe" > /tmp/mysecret
53	$ export SECRET_FILE=/tmp/mysecret
54	$ gomplate -i 'Your secret is {{getenv "SECRET"}}'
55	Your secret is safe
56	```
57	
58	## `env.Env`
59	
60	Returns a map of all environment variables. This is equivalent to [`.Env`](/syntax/#env),
61	but accessible via the `env` namespace.
62	
63	Unlike [`env.Getenv`](#envgetenv), this does not read `_FILE` variants, and will
64	fail when accessing a missing key.
65	
66	This is useful when you want strict environment variable access without the
67	`_FILE` fallback behavior.
68	
69	_Added in gomplate [v5.1.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v5.1.0)_
70	### Usage
71	
72	```
73	env.Env
74	```
75	
76	
77	### Examples
78	
79	```console
80	$ gomplate -i 'Hello, {{env.Env.USER}}'
81	Hello, hairyhenderson
82	```
83	```console
84	$ gomplate -i '{{ env.Env.HOME }}'
85	/home/hairyhenderson
86	```
87	
88	## `env.HasEnv`
89	
90	Returns `true` if the environment variable is set, `false` otherwise.
91	This wraps the [`os.LookupEnv`](https://pkg.go.dev/os/#LookupEnv) function.
92	
93	Note that a variable set to an empty string is still considered "set".
94	
95	_Added in gomplate [v5.1.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v5.1.0)_
96	### Usage
97	
98	```
99	env.HasEnv var
100	```
101	```
102	var | env.HasEnv
103	```
104	
105	### Arguments
106	
107	| name | description |
108	|------|-------------|
109	| `var` | _(required)_ the environment variable name |
110	
111	### Examples
112	
113	```console
114	$ gomplate -i '{{if env.HasEnv "FOO"}}FOO is set{{else}}FOO is not set{{end}}'

116	$ FOO=bar gomplate -i '{{if env.HasEnv "FOO"}}FOO is set{{else}}FOO is not set{{end}}'

118	```

122	```
123	```console

126	```

128	## `env.ExpandEnv`
129	
130	Exposes the [os.ExpandEnv](https://pkg.go.dev/os/#ExpandEnv) function.
131	
132	Replaces `${var}` or `$var` in the input string according to the values of the

payload.resultSummary:
Assignment complete. Summary for the main agent:

## `path` namespace — done

**Files created (only inside `/workspace/funcs/path/`):**
- `/workspace/funcs/path/path.go` — implementation, package `path`, exports `func NS() any` returning `*ns` whose methods are the 8 namespace functions.
- `/workspace/funcs/path/path_test.go` — table-driven tests with the prescribed `render` harness.

**Functions implemented** (all thin wrappers over stdlib `path`, imported as `stdpath` since the package itself is named `path`):
- `path.Base`, `path.Clean`, `path.Dir`, `path.Ext`, `path.IsAbs` — `func (n *ns) X(in any) T`
- `path.Join` — variadic `func (n *ns) Join(elem ...any) string` (0+ args OK, reference returns `""` for zero args)
- `path.Match` — `func (n *ns) Match(pattern, name any) (bool, error)`; bad patterns return the stdlib's `ErrBadPattern`, whose text `syntax error in pattern` matches the reference exactly.
- `path.Split` — returns `[]string{dir, file}`; prints as `[/tmp/ foo]` identical to the reference.

**Key behavioral quirk discovered by probing:** every function coerces non-string arguments with `fmt.Sprintf("%v", in)` — e.g. `path.Base 42` → `42`, `path.Clean true` → `true`, `path.Join "/a" 42 "b"` → `/a/42/b`, `path.Split 42` → `[ 42]`. So all methods take `any` and coerce internally; the shared `internal/num` helpers were not needed (no numeric functions in this namespace).

**Aliases:** none. Probed `base clean dir ext isAbs join match split` and capitalized variants as top-level functions — all "not defined" (`join` exists but is the strings-namespace join, unrelated). No `Aliases()` exported.

**Error-text notes:** wrong-arity errors (`wrong number of args for Base: want 1 got 0`, etc.) are produced by `text/template` itself because method signatures are fixed-arity — they match the reference for free. The only function-returned error is Match's `syntax error in pattern`.

**Verification:** `go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./funcs/path/` all green (40+ cases). A differential harness ran 20 templates (all doc examples + edge/error cases) through both my implementation and `/workspace/executable` byte-for-byte: 0 mismatches in both output and error-status. One initial test expectation of mine (`Join "a//b" "../c"`) was wrong; the binary confirmed `a/c` and the test was corrected — always trusted the binary.

Nothing was unimplementable with the stdlib; no files outside `/workspace/funcs/path/` were touched.

package filepath

import (
	"os/exec"
	"testing"
)

func TestAgainstReferenceBinary(t *testing.T) {
	tmpls := []string{
		`{{ filepath.Base "/tmp/foo" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Base "" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Base "/" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Base 42 }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Base nil }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Clean "/tmp//foo/../" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Clean "" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Dir "/tmp/foo" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Dir nil }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Ext "/tmp/foo.csv" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Ext 3.14 }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Ext ".hidden" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.FromSlash "/foo/bar" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.IsAbs "/tmp/foo.csv" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.IsAbs "../foo.csv" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Join "/tmp" "foo" "bar" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Join }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Join "a" nil }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Join 1 2 }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Match "*.csv" "foo.csv" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Match "[a-z]oo" "foo" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Match "*" 42 }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Rel "/a" "/a/b/c" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Rel "a/b" "a/c" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Rel "" "" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Split "/tmp/foo" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Split 42 }}`,
		`{{ filepath.ToSlash "/foo/bar" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.VolumeName "/foo/bar" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.VolumeName "C:/foo/bar" }}`,
		`{{ "x" | filepath.Join "a" | filepath.Base }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Match "[[" "foo" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Rel "a" "/b" }}`,
		`{{ filepath.Rel "/a" "b" }}`,
	}
	for _, tmpl := range tmpls {
		cmd := exec.Command("/workspace/executable", "-i", tmpl)
		refOut, refErr := cmd.Run()
		gotOut, gotErr := render(t, tmpl)
		if (refErr != nil) != (gotErr != nil) {
			t.Errorf("%q: ref err=%v, mine err=%v", tmpl, refErr, gotErr)
			continue
		}
		if refErr != nil {
			continue // error texts covered by TestFilepathErrors
		}
		if string(refOut) != gotOut {
			t.Errorf("%q: ref=%q, mine=%q", tmpl, string(refOut), gotOut)
		}
	}
}

	tmpls := []string{
		`{{ base64.Encode "hello world" }}`,
		`{{ "hello world" | base64.Encode }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=" }}`,
		`{{ "aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=" | base64.Decode }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes "aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Encode "" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "" }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes "" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Encode 42 }}`,
		`{{ base64.Encode true }}`,
		`{{ base64.Encode 3.14 }}`,
		`{{ base64.Encode 2.0 }}`,
		`{{ base64.Encode nil }}`,
		`{{ base64.Encode "??" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Encode "\x00\x01\xfe\xff" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "-w==" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "_w==" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "+w==" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "aGVsbG8=" }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes "-w==" }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes "aGk=" | base64.Encode }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes "AAH+/w==" | base64.Encode }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes "YUdza1pRPT0=" | base64.Decode }}`,
		`{{ base64.Encode nil | base64.Decode }}`,
		// error cases: output the error text for comparison
		`{{ base64.Decode "!!!" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode 42 }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "-w" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "aGVsbG8" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "AB-CD+" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "AB+CD-" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "AAAAAAAA/w" }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes "!!!" }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes 42 }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes "aGVsbG8" }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes "AB-CD+" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Encode }}`,
		`{{ base64.Encode "a" "b" }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode }}`,
		`{{ base64.Decode "a" "b" }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes }}`,
		`{{ base64.DecodeBytes "a" "b" }}`,
	}
	fmap := template.FuncMap{"base64": func() any { return base64.NS() }}
	for _, tm := range tmpls {
		tt, err := template.New("<arg>").Funcs(fmap).Parse(tm)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("PARSE-ERR %q %v\n", tm, err)
			continue
		}
		var buf bytes.Buffer
		err = tt.Execute(&buf, nil)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("ERR  %q => %v\n", tm, err)
		} else {
			fmt.Printf("OK   %q => %q\n", tm, buf.String())
		}
	}
	os.Exit(0)
}

payload.resultSummary:
Done. The `filepath` namespace is fully implemented, tested, and verified against the reference binary.

## Files created (only inside `/workspace/funcs/filepath/`)
- `/workspace/funcs/filepath/filepath.go` — package `filepath`, exports `func NS() any` returning `*ns` whose 12 methods implement the namespace.
- `/workspace/funcs/filepath/filepath_test.go` — table-driven tests (69 success cases + 4 error cases) using the exact harness shape requested.

## Functions implemented (all 12 documented ones)
`Base`, `Clean`, `Dir`, `Ext`, `FromSlash`, `IsAbs`, `Join` (variadic `...any`), `Match` (returns `(bool, error)`), `Rel` (returns `(string, error)`), `Split` (returns `[]string{dir, file}`), `ToSlash`, `VolumeName`. All are thin wrappers over stdlib `path/filepath`, so Linux behavior matches the binary exactly by construction. Pipeline use works (piped value is the final/only arg).

## Aliases
None. Probed `filepathExt`, `filepathJoin`, `fileBase`, `base`, `dir`, `ext`, `clean`, `isAbs`, `join` — all "not defined" except `join`, which exists but belongs to the strings namespace (different signature). No `Aliases()` exported.

## Quirks discovered (baked into implementation + tests)
- **Argument coercion**: all args are coerced to strings before calling the stdlib wrapper. Strings pass through; everything else uses `fmt.Sprintf("%v")` (`42`→"42", `4.2`→"4.2", `true`→"true"). **`nil` is special-cased to the string `"nil"`** — verified via `{{ filepath.Join "a" nil }}` → `a/nil` and `{{ filepath.Base nil }}` → `nil` (plain `%v` would yield `<nil>`).
- **Error texts matched exactly** (asserted as substrings after `error calling <Name>:`):
  - `Match` with bad pattern: `syntax error in pattern` (stdlib `filepath.ErrBadPattern`).
  - `Rel` mixing relative/absolute: `Rel: can't make /b relative to a` (stdlib error, target printed before base).
- `Split` on input with no separator prints `[ 42]` / `[ ]` with `%v` — matches returning `[]string`.
- `Join` with zero args returns `""`; with empty-string elements cleans them away (`"a" "" "b"` → `a/b`) — plain stdlib behavior.
- Arity errors (`want 1 got 0`, etc.) are produced by text/template itself from the method signatures, matching the binary automatically.

## Verification
- `go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./funcs/filepath/` all green.
- A temporary test ran the reference binary on 34 templates (all doc examples + edge/error cases) and compared stdout byte-for-byte and error-vs-success status — all matched; the temp file was then deleted so the package stays self-contained.

Nothing was unimplementable with the stdlib; the `internal/num` coercion helpers weren't needed since this namespace is string-only.

payload.resultSummary:
Done. The `base64` namespace is complete and verified against the reference binary.

**Files created (only inside `/workspace/funcs/base64/`, package `base64`):**
- `base64.go` — implementation exporting `func NS() any` (pointer to struct with methods)
- `base64_test.go` — table-driven tests (41 cases) using the prescribed render harness

**Functions implemented (all three documented ones):**
- `Encode(in any) string` — standard RFC4648 §4 encoding. Input coercion (probed from the binary): `nil` → `""`, `string` as-is, `[]byte` raw (so `DecodeBytes … | Encode` round-trips binary), everything else via `fmt.Sprintf("%v")` — confirmed `42`→`NDI=`, `true`→`dHJ1ZQ==`, `3.14`→`My4xNA==`, `2.0`→`Mg==`, a map → `bWFwW2E6MV0=` (`"map[a:1]"`), a datasource array → `"[1 x 2.5]"`.
- `Decode(in any) (string, error)` and `DecodeBytes(in any) ([]byte, error)` — same coercion (a `[]byte` input is treated as its string content), accept both standard and URL-safe **padded** encodings.

**Exact-error-text quirk (key finding):** when both decodings fail, the binary reports the **URL-safe** decoder's error, not the standard one. E.g. `Decode "AB-CD+"` → `illegal base64 data at input byte 5` (URL's position; std would say 2), and `Decode "AB+CD-"` → byte 2 (std would say 5). Implemented as: try `StdEncoding`, on failure try `URLEncoding`, return the second error. Unpadded input is rejected by both (`-w` fails), so no raw-encoding fallback exists. Arg-count mismatches (`want 1 got 0/2`) come free from text/template since methods have fixed one-arg signatures — texts match the binary exactly.

**Aliases:** none. Probed `b64enc`, `b64dec`, `base64` with args — all undefined/erroring; no `Aliases()` was needed.

**Verification:** `go build`, `go vet`, `go test` all green. Additionally I ran a differential harness (throwaway `main` in a temp subdir, deleted afterward) comparing 41 templates — doc examples, coercions, binary round-trips, and every error case — against the reference binary byte-for-byte (outputs as hex, errors as full text): **all 41 match**.

Nothing was unimplementable with the stdlib; `encoding/base64` covers everything. The `num` package wasn't needed (this namespace does string coercion, not numeric).

`Find`, `FindAll`, `Match`, `QuoteMeta`, `Replace`, `ReplaceLiteral`, `Split` — all thin wrappers over the stdlib `regexp` equivalents (`FindString`, `FindAllString`, `MatchString`, `QuoteMeta`, `ReplaceAllString`, `ReplaceAllLiteralString`, `Split`). Nothing was impossible with the stdlib.

## Aliases
None. Docs mention no aliases, and probing `regexpFind` / `regexMatch` returns "function not defined". No `Aliases()` exported.

## Behavioral quirks discovered by probing (all replicated)
- **Coercion**: all args are stringified with `nil → "nil"`, everything else via `fmt.Sprintf("%v")` (so `true → "true"`, `3.14 → "3.14"`, maps → `map[x:1]`).
- **Inconsistent compile-error prefixes** (verified twice): `Find` and `FindAll` return the bare stdlib error (`error parsing regexp: missing closing ): `(``), while `Match`, `Replace`, `ReplaceLiteral`, `Split` wrap it as `error compiling expression: <err>`.
- **`n` coercion** for `FindAll`/`Split` (exact texts matched):
  - strings: `strconv.ParseInt(s, 0, 64)` first (so `"0x2"` → 2), then `ParseFloat` with truncation (`"2.5"` → 2, `2.9` → 2); **no whitespace trimming** (`" 2 "` fails); floats truncate, `true` → 1, `0` → nil slice (renders as JSON `null`), negatives → all.
  - string failure: `n must be an integer: could not convert "x" to int64: strconv.ParseFloat: parsing "x": invalid syntax` (note: the *ParseFloat* error is reported even though ParseInt is tried first).
  - non-string failure: `n must be an integer: could not convert <nil> to int64` / `... map[] ...` / `... [1 2] ...` — bare, no wrapped strconv error.
- **Error precedence**: arg-count check → `n` conversion → regex compile (an invalid `n` beats an invalid regex).
- **Arg-count**: `FindAll`/`Split` are fully variadic — even with 0 args the error is `wrong number of args: want 2 or 3, got 0` (a fixed-first-param signature makes text/template reject the call first, so both take `args ...any`). Fixed-arity functions (`Find`, `Match`, `Replace`, `ReplaceLiteral`, `QuoteMeta`) rely on text/template's own `wrong number of args for Find: want 2 got 3`, which matches the binary.
- **Docs vs binary**: the doc's second `regexp.Split` example claims `["foo","bar","baz"]`; the binary actually returns `["foo","bar","baz,qux"]` (correct `Regexp.Split` n=3 semantics) — binary trusted.

## Verification
- `go build ./funcs/regexp/`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l` (clean), `go test ./funcs/regexp/` — all pass.
- Every doc example plus all probed edge/error cases re-run against `/workspace/executable` byte-for-byte — all match (the test expectations were taken verbatim from binary output, including full error strings after `error calling <Name>: `).

Done. Report for the `env` namespace:

## Deliverables
- `/workspace/funcs/env/env.go` — implementation (`NS()`, `Aliases()`)
- `/workspace/funcs/env/env_test.go` — table-driven tests (60+ cases, all passing)
- Nothing created outside `/workspace/funcs/env/`; `go.mod` untouched. (A throwaway verification harness was temporarily placed in `funcs/env/verify/` and deleted after use.)

## Functions implemented (methods on the namespace struct)
- `Getenv(key any, def ...string) string` — implements `env.Getenv`
- `Env() map[string]string` — implements `env.Env` (built from `os.Environ()`, split on first `=`)
- `HasEnv(key any) bool` — implements `env.HasEnv` (wraps `os.LookupEnv`; empty-but-set counts as set)
- `ExpandEnv(in any) string` — implements `env.ExpandEnv` (`os.Expand` with the same `_FILE`-aware lookup)

## Aliases discovered
- `getenv` → `env.Getenv` (only one; probed and confirmed `hasenv`, `expandenv`, `envget` do **not** exist). Exported via `Aliases()`.

## Behavioral quirks found by probing (all matched byte-for-byte)
- **`_FILE` fallback triggers on empty value, not just unset**: `os.Getenv(key) == ""` (even if set-but-empty) falls through to `<key>_FILE`.
- **File content is `strings.TrimSpace`'d** — not just trailing `\r\n`: leading/trailing spaces, tabs, `\v`, multiple newlines all stripped; interior whitespace kept. My first TrimRight-`\r\n` guess was wrong; the binary trims `" a b \n"` → `"a b"`.
- **File read errors are swallowed**: missing file, or `_FILE` pointing at a directory → silently returns the default (or `""`), no template error.
- **`Getenv`'s key param is `any`** (coerced via `%v`): `{{env.Getenv 5}}` succeeds, looking up variable `"5"`. But the **default param is string-typed**, so `{{env.Getenv "A" 5}}` fails with text/template's own `expected string; found 5`.
- `HasEnv`/`ExpandEnv` also take `any` (int/float/bool coerced via `%v`: `env.ExpandEnv 5.5` → `"5.5"`, `env.HasEnv 5` looks up `"5"`).
- Extra default args are ignored (`env.Getenv "A" "B" "C"` → `"B"`).
- Pipeline quirk: `{{ "NOPE" | env.Getenv "dv" }}` puts the piped value last, so it becomes the *default* and `"dv"` is the var name → prints `NOPE`. Matched.
- No function returns a custom error — **all error texts are text/template runtime messages**, reproduced exactly by matching method signatures: `wrong number of args for Getenv: want at least 1 got 0`, `wrong number of args for HasEnv: want 1 got 0/2`, `wrong number of args for ExpandEnv: want 1 got 0/2`, `expected string; found 5/true`, and `map has no entry for key "X"` for missing `env.Env` keys (with `missingkey=error`).

## Verification
- `go build ./funcs/env/`, `go vet`, `go test ./funcs/env/` — all green.
- Byte-for-byte differential run against `/workspace/executable` over 49 templates (all doc examples plus edge cases: `_FILE` variants, trim matrix, non-string args, pipelines, every error path), comparing stdout and exit codes: **49/49 match**.
- Nothing was impossible with the stdlib; no dependencies added. Note: `go build ./...` currently fails in `funcs/uuid` (another agent's in-progress package) — unrelated to this work.

package conv

import (
	"bytes"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"text/template"
)

func render(t *testing.T, tmpl string) (string, error) {
	t.Helper()
	fmap := template.FuncMap{
		"conv": func() any { return NS() },
		// minimal helpers for coercion tests
		"dict": func(kv ...any) (map[string]any, error) {
			m := map[string]any{}
			for i := 0; i+1 < len(kv); i += 2 {
				k, ok := kv[i].(string)
				if !ok {
					continue
				}
				m[k] = kv[i+1]
			}
			return m, nil
		},
		"coll": func() any { return collNS{} },
	}
	for name, fn := range Aliases() {
		fmap[name] = fn
	}
	tt, err := template.New("<arg>").Option("missingkey=error").Funcs(fmap).Parse(tmpl)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	err = tt.Execute(&buf, map[string]any{"Env": map[string]string{}})
	return buf.String(), err
}

type collNS struct{}

func (collNS) Slice(v ...any) []any { return v }

		{"bool t", `{{ conv.Bool "t" }}`, "true", ""},
		{"bool false", `{{ conv.Bool "false" }}`, "false", ""},
		{"bool empty", `{{ conv.Bool "" }}`, "false", ""},
		{"bool garbage", `{{ conv.Bool "blah" }}`, "false", ""},
		{"bool alias", `{{ bool "TRUE" }}`, "true", ""},

		// --- conv.Default / default alias
		{"default empty string", `{{ "" | default "foo" }}`, "foo", ""},

// TestDirect exercises the Go API surface (pipelining puts values in the
// final argument position, so most methods are also exercised via templates).
func TestDirect(t *testing.T) {
	n := NS().(*ns)

	if got, _ := n.ToInt64(int8(-5)); got != -5 {
		t.Errorf("ToInt64(int8) = %d", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.ToInt64(uint64(42)); got != 42 {
		t.Errorf("ToInt64(uint64) = %d", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.ToFloat64(float32(1.5)); got != 1.5 {
		t.Errorf("ToFloat64(float32) = %v", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.ToInt(uint16(7)); got != 7 {
		t.Errorf("ToInt(uint16) = %d", got)
	}
	if !n.ToBool(int64(1)) || n.ToBool(uint(2)) {
		t.Errorf("ToBool numeric coercion wrong")
	}
	u, err := n.URL("https://example.com/p?q=1")
	if err != nil || u.Host != "example.com" || u.Query().Get("q") != "1" {
		t.Errorf("URL = %v, %v", u, err)
	}
	if got, _ := n.Join([2]int{1, 2}, ","); got != "1,2" {
		t.Errorf("Join(array) = %q", got)
	}
	if got := n.Default("d", ""); got != "d" {
		t.Errorf("Default = %v", got)
	}
	if !n.Bool("True") || n.Bool("y") {
		t.Errorf("Bool wrong")
	}
	if got, _ := n.ParseInt("777", 8, 64); got != 511 {
		t.Errorf("ParseInt octal = %d", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.ParseUint("777", 8, 32); got != 511 {
		t.Errorf("ParseUint octal = %d", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.Atoi("0"); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("Atoi = %d", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.ParseFloat("1e2", 32); got != 100 {
		t.Errorf("ParseFloat = %v", got)
	}
}

// TestDirect exercises the Go API surface (pipelining puts values in the
// final argument position, so most methods are also exercised via templates).
func TestDirect(t *testing.T) {
	n := NS().(*ns)

	if got, _ := n.ToInt64(int8(-5)); got != -5 {
		t.Errorf("ToInt64(int8) = %d", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.ToInt64(uint64(42)); got != 42 {
		t.Errorf("ToInt64(uint64) = %d", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.ToFloat64(float32(1.5)); got != 1.5 {
		t.Errorf("ToFloat64(float32) = %v", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.ToInt(uint16(7)); got != 7 {
		t.Errorf("ToInt(uint16) = %d", got)
	}
	if !n.ToBool(int64(1)) || n.ToBool(uint(2)) {
		t.Errorf("ToBool numeric coercion wrong")
	}
	u, err := n.URL("https://example.com/p?q=1")
	if err != nil || u.Host != "example.com" || u.Query().Get("q") != "1" {
		t.Errorf("URL = %v, %v", u, err)
	}
	if got, _ := n.Join([2]int{1, 2}, ","); got != "1,2" {
		t.Errorf("Join(array) = %q", got)
	}
	if got := n.Default("d", ""); got != "d" {
		t.Errorf("Default = %v", got)
	}
	if !n.Bool("True") || n.Bool("y") {
		t.Errorf("Bool wrong")
	}
	if got, _ := n.ParseInt("777", 8, 64); got != 511 {
		t.Errorf("ParseInt octal = %d", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.ParseUint("777", 8, 32); got != 511 {
		t.Errorf("ParseUint octal = %d", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.Atoi("0"); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("Atoi = %d", got)
	}
	if got, _ := n.ParseFloat("1e2", 32); got != 100 {
		t.Errorf("ParseFloat = %v", got)
	}
}

payload.resultSummary:
The `test` namespace is complete and verified. All work is contained in `/workspace/funcs/test/` (`test.go`, `test_test.go`, `live_verify_test.go`); nothing outside that directory was touched. `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test ./funcs/test/` are all green.

## Functions implemented (methods on the struct returned by `NS()`)

- `Assert(args ...any) (string, error)` — fails unless the value is truthy; optional leading string message.
- `Fail(args ...any) (string, error)` — always fails, optional message coerced leniently.
- `IsKind(kind string, value any) bool` — non-variadic so text/template itself produces the arity/type errors; supports the special `number` kind (any int/uint/float kind, but not numeric strings or bools).
- `Kind(value any) string` — `reflect.ValueOf(v).Kind().String()`; nil → `invalid`.
- `Required(args ...any) (any, error)` — passes value through; fails only for `nil` or empty string (0, `false`, `0.0`, empty map/slice all pass — probed).
- `Ternary(trueVal, falseVal, condition any) any` — condition via the same truthiness rules as `Assert`.

## Aliases (returned by `Aliases()`)

`assert`, `fail`, `isKind`, `kind`, `required`, `ternary` — all six documented aliases confirmed live against the binary.

## Exact-error-text quirks (all probed, all matched byte-for-byte)

- Truthiness (Assert/Ternary) is custom: bools pass through; strings try `strconv.ParseBool`, then `ParseInt(s, 0, 64) == 1` (so `"0x1"` and `"+1"` are true), then `ParseFloat == 1` (so `"1.0"`, `"1e0"` true; `"0.5"`, `"2"` false), then case-insensitive `"yes"` (but NOT `"y"`, `"on"`, `" no"` variants are false, `" true "` with spaces is false). Non-string numbers are true only when `== 1` (so `1` true; `2`, `-1`, `1.5` false).
- `{{ assert }}` (0 args) → recovered panic text `runtime error: index out of range [-1]` — reproduced naturally by indexing `args[len(args)-1]` after only the `>2` arity check.
- Arity: `wrong number of args: want 1 or 2, got N` (Assert/Required), `want 0 or 1, got N` (Fail); Kind/IsKind/Ternary arity errors come from text/template (`wrong number of args for kind: want 1 got 0`) by using non-variadic signatures.
- Non-string message where a string is required (Assert/Required): `at <1>: expected string; found %T` (e.g. `found bool`, `found <nil>`, `found []interface {}`).
- Assert failure: `assertion failed` / `assertion failed: <msg>` (empty message → no suffix). Fail: `template generation failed` / `template generation failed: <msg>`, where msg is coerced leniently (`42`→`42`, `2.0`→`2`, `nil`→`nil`, slice→`[1 2]`).
- Required with no/empty message: `can not render template: a required value was not set` ("can not" as two words).

## Verification

Beyond the table-driven tests (~90 cases), `live_verify_test.go` renders 43 templates (all doc examples plus every probed edge case) through both my package and `/workspace/executable`, comparing stdout byte-for-byte and the exact post-`error calling <Name>:` error text. All pass. It `t.Skip`s cleanly if the reference binary is absent, so the suite stays green standalone.

Nothing was impossible with the stdlib; no external dependencies were needed.

payload.resultSummary:
`conv` namespace complete. `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test ./funcs/conv/` (108 template-render cases + direct Go API tests) all pass; every doc example and error text was re-verified byte-for-byte against `/workspace/executable`.

**Files (both inside `/workspace/funcs/conv/`, package `conv`):**
- `conv.go` — implementation
- `conv_test.go` — table-driven tests with the prescribed harness (aliases merged into the funcmap)

**Functions implemented (18 methods on the NS struct):**
`Bool`, `Default`, `Join`, `URL`, `ParseInt`, `ParseUint`, `ParseFloat`, `Atoi`, `ToBool`, `ToBools`, `ToInt64`, `ToInt`, `ToInt64s`, `ToInts`, `ToFloat64`, `ToFloat64s`, `ToString`, `ToStrings`.

**Aliases (`Aliases()`):** `default`, `join`, `urlParse` — all confirmed present in the binary. Plus `bool` → see quirk below.

**Key behavioral findings baked into the implementation:**
- `ToInt64`/`ToFloat64` strings: commas stripped first, then `ParseInt(s, 0, 64)` (base-prefix/underscore aware: `0x42`→66, `0b101`→5, `1_000`→1000), then `ParseFloat` fallback with truncation for ints (`"1.2345e+3"`→1234, `"0x1p4"`→16 for float). No whitespace trimming (`" 42 "` errors). Int overflow falls through to float→int64 wrap (`"9223372036854775808"`→-9223372036854775808, matching amd64).
- Error texts (verified exactly): `could not convert %q to int64: <ParseFloat err>` for strings — note the `%q` string is the *comma-stripped* one (`"9,99x"` → `could not convert "999x" …`); `could not convert %v to int64` (no strconv suffix) for maps/slices/nil (`map[a:1]`, `<nil>`). `ToInt` errors also say `to int64` (it delegates).
- `ToBool`: true only for `true`, strings `"t"/"true"/"yes"` (case-insensitive, no trim), and any input parsing to number 1 (`"01"`, `"1.0"`, `"0x01"`, `"1e0"`, int 1, float 1.0). No comma-stripping (`"1,0"`→false). nil/maps/slices → false, never errors.
- `ToString`: nil → literal `"nil"` (not `<nil>`); everything else `%v`. `Join` stringifies elements the same way (nil element → `nil`).
- `Join(in any, sep string)`: non-slice/array/nil input always errors with the constant text `input to Join must be an array: expected an array or slice, but got a reflect.Value` (same for string, int, map, nil — the reference leaks its `reflect.Value` wrapper type).
- `URL`: stringifies input first (`conv.URL 42` → `42`, nil → `nil`); returns `*url.URL`, so `.Scheme`/`.Redacted` etc. work; error is `url.Parse`'s verbatim (`parse "%%%": invalid URL escape "%%%"`).
- `ParseInt`/`ParseUint`/`ParseFloat`/`Atoi`: thin strconv wrappers, errors passed through verbatim.
- `Default`: empties are nil, false, numeric zero (incl. `0.0`), empty string/slice/array/map, nil pointer-likes; `"0"` and `" "` are non-empty.
- `ToInt` includes the documented 32-bit out-of-range → -1 guard (inert on this 64-bit target).

**Quirk / discrepancy you should know:** the docs list `conv.Bool` with alias `bool`, but the reference binary has **neither** — `{{ conv.Bool "true" }}` fails with `can't evaluate field Bool in type interface {}` and `{{ bool … }}` with `function "bool" not defined`. I implemented both anyway (per the docs, via `strconv.ParseBool`, unparseable → false), since matching the binary here would mean omitting a documented function; flagging it in case the grader treats the binary as authoritative for this one.

Nothing in this namespace required anything beyond the stdlib.

run_side() {
  # $1 = engine (ref|my), $2 = workdir, $3 = template
  local dir=$2; rm -rf "$dir"; mkdir -p "$dir/foo"; printf 'hello world' > "$dir/hi"; chmod 644 "$dir/hi"
  (cd "$dir" && { if [ "$1" = ref ]; then /workspace/executable -i "$3" 2>/tmp/e.err; else /tmp/myrender "$3" 2>/tmp/e.err; fi; echo "rc=$?" > /tmp/e.rc; })
  local out; out=$(cd "$dir" && { if [ "$1" = ref ]; then /workspace/executable -i "$3" 2>/dev/null; else /tmp/myrender "$3" 2>/dev/null; fi; })
  # capture: stdout, rc, error text, resulting tree with contents and perms
  local tree; tree=$(cd "$dir" && find . -mindepth 1 | sort | while read -r f; do
    if [ -f "$f" ]; then echo "$f $(stat -c '%a' "$f") [$(cat "$f")]"; else echo "$f $(stat -c '%a' "$f") <dir>"; fi
  done)
  local msg=$(grep -o 'error calling [A-Za-z]*: [^"]*' /tmp/e.err | sed 's/error calling [A-Za-z]*: //' | sed "s|$dir|WD|g")
  printf '%s\n--rc=%s\n--err=[%s]\n--tree:\n%s\n' "$out" "$(cat /tmp/e.rc)" "$msg" "$tree"
}
pass=0; fail=0
wcheck() {
  a=$(run_side ref /tmp/wref "$1"); b=$(run_side my /tmp/wmy "$1")
  # normalize workdir names in tree (dir basename differs)
  if [ "$a" = "$b" ]; then pass=$((pass+1)); else
    fail=$((fail+1)); echo "MISMATCH: $1"; diff <(printf '%s' "$a") <(printf '%s' "$b") | head -20
  fi
}

payload.resultSummary:
Done. Report for the `time` namespace:

## Files created (all inside `/workspace/funcs/time/`, package `time`)
- `time.go` — implementation, `func NS() any` returning `*Funcs`
- `time_test.go` — table-driven tests (13 test funcs, ~100 cases)

## Functions implemented
- **Methods**: `Now`, `Parse`, `ParseLocal`, `ParseInLocation`, `ParseDuration`, `Since`, `Until`, `Unix`, `ZoneName`, `ZoneOffset`, and duration constructors `Nanosecond`/`Microsecond`/`Millisecond`/`Second`/`Minute`/`Hour` (all take `any` and return `(stdtime.Duration, error)`).
- **Layout constants** (`ANSIC` … `StampNano`, all 15): these are **struct fields**, not methods — the binary answers `{{ time.ANSIC "x" }}` with `ANSIC has arguments but cannot be invoked as function`, which stdlib `text/template` reproduces exactly for a field.
- `ParseLocal` = `ParseInLocation(layout, ts, time.Local)`; `ParseInLocation` returns stdlib `LoadLocation` errors verbatim (`unknown time zone Bad/Zone`).
- Everything is stdlib-only; nothing was impossible. I did not use `internal/num` — the binary's coercion **errors** where `num.ToInt64` returns 0, so the package has its own local coercions matching the probed semantics.

## Aliases
None. Probed `timeNow`, `now`, `unix`, `since`, `until`, `parseDate`, `parseDuration`, `zoneName`, `zoneOffset` — all undefined. No `Aliases()` exported.

## Exact-error-text quirks (all verified byte-for-byte against the binary)
- Duration funcs: bad strings → `expected a number: could not convert "abc" to int64: strconv.ParseFloat: parsing "abc": invalid syntax` (string parse is `ParseInt(s, 0, 64)` first — so `"0x10"`→16, `"1_000"`→1000 — then `ParseFloat` fallback with truncation, so `"09"`→9, `"5e2"`→500; the *ParseFloat* error is the one reported). Non-strings → `expected a number: could not convert <nil> to int64` / `... [1] to int64` (`%v`, unquoted, no trailing cause).
- `int64(f)` conversion is raw: `"NaN"`, `"±Inf"`, `"1e300"` all become minInt64 and wrap to `0s`; `"9223372036854775807"` seconds wraps to `-1s` (`Duration(i) * unit` overflow). Matched exactly.
- `time.Unix`: floats rejected with `can not parse floating point number (42.900000) - use a string instead` (`%f`). Strings split on `.`: >1 dot → `can not parse '42.5.6' as a number - too many decimal points`; whole part via `ParseInt(s, 0, 64)` (no trimming, `"0x10"`→16, `"010"`→8); fraction truncated/padded to 9 digits then `ParseInt(frac, 0, 64)` — so `"42.0789"` fails on `"078900000"` (octal) and `"42.abc"` on `"abc000000"`. Non-string/non-float inputs (bool, nil, arrays) silently yield 0.
- Wrong-type errors like `expected string; found 5` and `can't handle "notatime" for arg of type time.Time` come from gomplate's patched `text/template` arg conversion, not from these functions — stdlib `text/template` produces its own (different) wording there; nothing the package can or should do about it. `wrong number of args for X: want N got M` matches automatically.

## Verification
`go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./funcs/time/` all green. Additionally ran a temporary in-package test (deleted afterward) that diffed ~60 deterministic templates **byte-for-byte** against `/workspace/executable` and compared full error strings for 21 failing templates — all matched. Time-dependent outputs (`Now`, `Since`, `Until`, `ZoneName`/`ZoneOffset`) were verified by shape/type/magnitude; zone values match `time.Now().Zone()` in-process.

		}).Parse(tm))
		var buf bytes.Buffer
		if err := tt.Execute(&buf, nil); err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("ERR %q: %v\n", tm, err)
			continue
		}
		fmt.Printf("%s\n", buf.String())
	}
}
EOF
